facts.summary: Arizona has no state overtime statute; overtime is governed solely by the federal FLSA (time-and-a-half after 40 hours per week), with no daily overtime or higher state salary threshold.
facts.citation: No Arizona overtime statute (federal FLSA, 29 U.S.C. 207 controls)
facts.sourceAgency: Industrial Commission of Arizona, Labor Department
facts.notes: Arizona wage law does not address overtime; the ICA administers minimum wage and paid sick time only. Verify FAQ page still states no state overtime provision.

facts.summary: Arizona's minimum wage is $15.15 per hour effective January 1, 2026, indexed annually to inflation and well above the federal $7.25.
facts.citation: A.R.S. 23-363 (Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act)
facts.sourceAgency: Industrial Commission of Arizona, Labor Department
facts.notes: Increased from $14.70 to $15.15 (+$0.45) based on CPI. Employers may take a tip credit of up to $3.00/hr under A.R.S. 23-363(C), making the tipped minimum $12.15/hr for 2026 — verify tipped figure directly on the ICA page (azica.gov blocked automated fetch; figure confirmed via ICA search summary and statutory tip-credit amount).

facts.summary: The Arizona Civil Rights Act mirrors federal law, prohibiting employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), age (40+), national origin, and disability; Arizona adds no additional statewide protected classes.
facts.sourceAgency: Arizona Attorney General, Civil Rights Division (FEPA)
facts.notes: No statewide protection for sexual orientation or gender identity in employment; some Arizona municipalities (e.g., Phoenix, Tucson) add local protections. Verify current ACRA class list.

facts.summary: For sexual harassment claims (and retaliation for opposing sexual harassment), the Arizona Civil Rights Act covers employers with one or more employees — far below the general 15-employee threshold that otherwise matches federal Title VII.
facts.notes: General ACRA coverage is 15+ employees (same as federal). The 1-employee threshold is specific to sexual harassment / retaliation-for-opposing-harassment claims.

facts.summary: The Arizona Employment Protection Act prohibits terminating employees for refusing to violate the law, reporting statutory violations in a reasonable manner, exercising workers' compensation rights, jury or military service, or voting.
facts.notes: Codifies wrongful-termination exceptions to at-will employment; where a statute provides its own remedy, that remedy is exclusive.

facts.value: 1 year for an administrative wage claim or a general unpaid-wages civil suit; 2 years (3 years if willful) for a civil action under the Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act
facts.summary: An administrative wage claim (capped at $12,000) filed with the Industrial Commission's Labor Department must be filed within one year of accrual (A.R.S. 23-356). A civil suit for general unpaid wages/treble damages under A.R.S. 23-355 also runs one year, borrowed from Arizona's catch-all one-year period for liability created by statute (A.R.S. 12-541(5)). But a separate civil action to enforce Arizona's minimum-wage and earned-paid-sick-time law (the Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act) has its own, longer limitations period: it may be commenced up to 2 years after a violation, or 3 years for a willful violation, and can reach a continuing course of violations regardless of date (A.R.S. 23-364(H)).
facts.citation: A.R.S. 23-356 (administrative claim, 1 year, $12,000 cap); A.R.S. 12-541(5) (general statutory-liability catch-all, 1 year, applied to A.R.S. 23-355 civil wage suits); A.R.S. 23-364(H) (Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act civil action, 2 years / 3 years if willful)
facts.notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-10: the prior version applied a blanket '1 year' (A.R.S. 23-356 / 12-541) to all wage claims, including minimum-wage claims. That is the correct period for (a) an administrative claim filed with the ICA Labor Department under A.R.S. 23-356 (1 year, $12,000 cap) and (b) a general civil suit for unpaid wages/treble damages under A.R.S. 23-355, which sets no limitations period of its own so courts apply the 1-year catch-all in A.R.S. 12-541(5) for 'liability created by statute.' But it is NOT correct for a civil action to enforce the Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act (Arizona's minimum-wage and earned-paid-sick-time law): A.R.S. 23-364(H) sets its own explicit civil statute of limitations of 2 years, extended to 3 years for a willful violation, confirmed against the enrolled text at azleg.gov ('A civil action to enforce this article may be commenced no later than two years after a violation last occurs, or three years in the case of a willful violation... The statute of limitations shall be tolled during any investigation of an employer by the commission...'). Section 23-364(H) governs minimum-wage and paid-sick-time claims specifically; A.R.S. 23-355/12-541 remains the operative 1-year period for other unpaid-wage claims (e.g., late regular pay, unlawful deductions) that are not minimum-wage/EPST claims. VERIFY periodically for amendment; the administrative $12,000 cap and 1-year figures should also be re-confirmed on the ICA site.

facts.summary: A discrimination charge must be filed with the Arizona Civil Rights Division within 180 days after the alleged unlawful employment practice occurred.
facts.sourceAgency: Arizona Attorney General, Civil Rights Division (FEPA)
facts.notes: State FEPA deadline is 180 days (shorter than the 300-day federal deadline available via EEOC in deferral states). Back pay does not accrue more than two years before filing.

facts.value: discharge: 7 working days or end of next pay period, whichever is sooner; quit: next regular payday
facts.summary: A discharged employee must be paid all wages within seven working days or by the end of the next regular pay period (whichever is sooner); an employee who quits is paid by the next regular payday.
facts.notes: Federal FLSA has no comparable final-pay deadline, so this is a state addition. Violation is a petty offense.

facts.summary: Arizona requires employers to provide earned paid sick time (accrued at one hour per 30 hours worked) under the Fair Wages and Healthy Families Act — a benefit with no federal equivalent.
facts.sourceAgency: Industrial Commission of Arizona, Labor Department
facts.notes: Accrual rate (one hour per 30 hours worked) and caps of 40 hours/year (employers with 15+ employees) or 24 hours/year (fewer than 15) are set by A.R.S. 23-372; A.R.S. 23-373 covers permitted uses only (citation corrected from 23-373 to 23-372). Verify current accrual caps on the ICA FAQ page.
